nodes.description: Public mapping(uint => address) storing the address of every gambler; source of recipient addresses for all payouts.
uint8 counter of currently registered players; incremented on each deposit and decremented inside refund/round-shift loops, so it can underflow.
uint bet size per player in wei (0.01 ether by default); drives every payout calculation.
uint8 number of sign-ups that trigger a draw; also used as modulus for the pseudo-random winner selection.
uint8 carry-over count of players rolled into the next round after a draw.
uint storing the pseudo-random winner index derived from block.blockhash(block.number).
uint percentage of the pot paid to the winner (default 90); remainder is split between two hard-coded addresses.
address of the contract deployer; used as the only authorisation check in changeParameters and refund.
uint block number captured when the required player count is reached; compared against block.number to decide the draw block.
Constructor: sets owner = msg.sender and initialises ante, required_number_players and winner_percentage.
Owner-only setter for ante, required_number_players and winner_percentage.
Owner-only refund routine that drains the contract balance to gamblers via transfer() inside a while loop.
Payable anonymous deposit function: registers the sender, triggers the draw when enough players joined, computes a pseudo-random winner and pays out the winner plus two fixed addresses.
msg.sender: attacker-controlled caller used for owner assignment, owner checks and gambler registration.
gamblers[player_count].transfer(ante) in refund(): external value transfer whose recipient index is taken from a decrementing counter (underflow/out-of-range recipient).
gamblers[1].transfer(this.balance) in refund(): sends the whole contract balance to a fixed mapping slot irrespective of that slot's real owner.
random = uint(block.blockhash(block.number))%required_number_players + 1: predictable block-hash based pseudo-randomness used to pick the winner.
gamblers[random].transfer(ante*required_number_players*winner_percentage/100): pays the pseudo-randomly chosen gambler the winner share of the pot.
0xBdf8fF4648bF66c03160F572f67722cf9793cE6b.transfer(...): sends half of the remaining (non-winner) pot to a hard-coded address.
0xA7aa3509d62B9f8B6ee02EA0cFd3738873D3ee4C.transfer(...): sends the other half of the remaining (non-winner) pot to a hard-coded address.
player_count -=1 inside the refund() while loop: uint8 arithmetic that can underflow to 255.
player_count +=1 on every deposit: uint8 arithmetic that can overflow after 255 deposits.
Parameter of changeParameters: the new ante value written into the ante state variable.
Parameter of changeParameters: the new required_number_players value.
Parameter of changeParameters: the new winner_percentage value.

edges.reason: Constructor writes the untrusted caller into the privileged owner state variable (owner = msg.sender).
The anonymous payable function stores msg.sender as gamblers[player_count], so caller-controlled addresses end up as payout recipients.
changeParameters gates all parameter updates on msg.sender == owner, an equality check on an untrusted caller.
owner (set from msg.sender at construction) is the only address allowed to modify ante/required_number_players/winner_percentage.
refund() is reachable only when msg.sender == owner, so authorisation depends entirely on the untrusted caller.
owner guards the balance-draining refund routine.
The ante state variable determines the value transferred in refund().
player_count is used as the mapping index (gamblers[player_count]) whose address receives the transfer.
The gamblers mapping supplies the recipient address of the refund transfer.
gamblers[1] from the mapping is the recipient of the full-balance refund transfer.
The player_count state variable is decremented, and uint8 underflow wraps it to 255 when the loop runs past zero.
The decremented value is written back into the player_count state variable inside the refund loop.
Deposits read and increment player_count (+=1), which can overflow the uint8 counter.
The incremented counter is stored back to the player_count state variable on each payable call.
bet_blocknumber is compared against block.number to decide whether the draw happens in the current block.
required_number_players is the modulus in the pseudo-random winner index computation.
The value computed by the pseudo-random expression determines which gambler index is paid.
The random state variable (winner index) selects gamblers[random] as the payout recipient.
The gamblers mapping provides the winner address that receives the pot share.
ante is a factor of the winner payout amount ante*required_number_players*winner_percentage/100.
required_number_players scales the pot size in the winner payout computation.
winner_percentage determines the winner's share of the pot in the payout expression.
ante appears in the residual pot amount sent to the first hard-coded address.
required_number_players scales the total pot in the residual fee calculation.
winner_percentage is subtracted out to derive the residual amount paid to the first hard-coded address.
ante appears in the residual pot amount sent to the second hard-coded address.
required_number_players scales the total pot in the residual fee calculation.
winner_percentage is subtracted out to derive the residual amount paid to the second hard-coded address.
The payable fallback function executes the winner transfer when the draw conditions are met.
The payable fallback function executes the first hard-coded fee transfer.
The payable fallback function executes the second hard-coded fee transfer.
Value transfer to gamblers[player_count] happens before player_count is decremented, so the recipient can re-enter refund() with stale counter state.
Full-balance transfer to gamblers[1] is an external call that can re-enter the refund routine before state settles.
Payout to gamblers[random] occurs before player_count/next_round_players are rewritten in the fallback loop, allowing re-entry into the payable function.
External transfer to the fixed fee address happens before the round-shift bookkeeping completes, so re-entry into the fallback is possible.
External transfer to the second fixed fee address happens before player_count is normalised, enabling re-entrant deposits.
The newAnte parameter is written directly into the ante state variable.
The newNumberOfPlayers parameter is written into required_number_players.
The newWinnerPercentage parameter is written into winner_percentage.

normalization_plan.reason: newAnte is only used as a temporary input that is immediately copied into the ante state variable inside changeParameters, so it carries no independent semantic meaning.
newNumberOfPlayers is a transient argument that is stored into required_number_players within changeParameters and never used elsewhere.
newWinnerPercentage is a transient argument that is stored into winner_percentage within changeParameters and never used elsewhere.
